source_reference.seed: roguelike-deckbuilder / single-character-roguelike-deckbuilder / Slay the Spire / PC Steam / tense-tactical

conventions.statement: Player efficacy = planning + luck landing together. The genre is fun when deliberate plans meet bounded randomness — the player rolls luck, luck does not happen to the player.
Anti-dominant-strategy: encounter/enemy variety so no single deck always wins; balance buffs underpicked options toward diversity.
Bounded, transparent RNG — randomness is constrained and visible; the player allocates it (e.g. roll dice then place them) rather than being a victim of it.
Cards-as-puzzle-pieces with combo/synergy payoff — the anticipated synergy landing is the core reward ('poggable moment' / well-oiled Rube Goldberg machine).
Energy economy — cards cost a limited per-turn resource forcing selection (commonly 3 energy/turn in StS lineage).
Deck-thinning / card-removal as a core lever — decks improve by removing weak cards, not only adding; prevents deck bloat diluting consistency.
Relics / permanent run-modifiers that fundamentally reshape how the deck functions; deck strategy synergizes with relic effects.
Metrics/analytics-driven balance — measure card pick-rate, buff underpicked cards toward diversity so no card is dead or dominant.
Map/path node choice — semi-random map; the player charts their route, weighing risk vs reward per node (which encounters to seek/avoid). FTL lineage.
Permadeath with a meta-progression cushion — a run ends on death, but cross-run unlocks (new cards/relics/characters) soften the loss so progress is felt.
No wasted resources — every action/resource must feel positive; leftover unused resources feel bad, so design ensures each is spendable ('having dice left over is the worst feeling').
One run is bounded and completable in a sitting (~30-60 min). NOT a ≤5min session genre — long-session by nature.

anti_tropes.statement: Dominant strategy / 'always pick the same thing' — a single optimal deck path that kills replayability.
Unfair/opaque RNG — randomness the player cannot see, plan around, or mitigate; luck happens TO the player.
Deck bloat with no thinning — decks only grow, diluting consistency; no removal lever.

pillars.name: 계획과 운이 만나는 순간 (Plans meeting luck)
pillars.anti_example: 플레이어가 보지도 못하고 대비도 못하는 RNG — 운이 나한테 일어난다는 느낌 (A2).

pillars.name: 언제나 다른 최적해 (No single right answer)
pillars.anti_example: 매번 같은 걸 고르는 게 최적 → 깨진 게임 (A1).

pillars.name: 시너지 빌드업 (Synergy build-up payoff)
pillars.anti_example: 덱이 불어나기만 하고 덜어낼 수단 없음 → 일관성 희석 (A3).

modules.name: Single-combat encounter (one fight, draw-play-resolve loop)
modules.playable_html: A single turn-based combat: hand of cards, energy per turn, play cards vs one enemy with telegraphed intent, win/lose. Proves planning+luck and synergy in ≤5min — also the narrowing path for the session-length eligibility miss.

modules.name: Map-node run structure (chart a route through a semi-random map)
modules.playable_html: A node map; player picks path weighing risk/reward per node, chains combats, permadeath ends the run.

modules.name: Deck-thinning + relic economy (between-combat deck refinement)
modules.playable_html: Post-combat reward screen: add a card OR remove a card OR take a relic; deck refines toward a synergy over a short run.
